title: This week in India's growth story.
caption:
This week in India's growth story: 35 stories covering history, sectors and mindset.

1. Ten Indians. One 246-year-old American academy. Same year.
2. 2026: An Indian-origin engineer is about to run Adobe for the second time in a row.
3. She lost her sight in childhood. Two decades later, she became the officer running the show.
4. September 21, 1994: India lost the industrialist who called himself "Gandhi's coolie" - and left behind a blueprint for honest business.
5. For decades, India's best researchers left and rarely came back. In June 2026, the government put ₹200 crore on the table to reverse that.
6. 2026: An Indian-origin executive with zero gaming experience now runs Xbox.
7. She was born without arms. At 17, she became the best archer on Earth.
8. September 22, 1991: India lost the widow who broke a taboo and reshaped who could act on screen.
9. He began his career as an engineer in a refrigerator factory. In 2026, he won one of science's most prestigious prizes - for changing how the world understands climate change.
10. India just launched its first fully indigenous ocean research vessel - built to work in six kilometres of water, in the roughest seas on the planet.
11. Most bone grafts used in India are still imported. A Maharashtra company just got government backing to 3D-print them here instead.
12. He already holds India's highest literary honor. In April 2026, America gave him one of its own.
13. A US visa rejection couldn't stop him. NASA came looking for him instead.
14. Married at 16 to escape poverty. Today she's the state's first woman joint director.
15. September 23, 1908: India's "National Poet" was born to a farmer in rural Bihar.
16. Making green hydrogen usually needs platinum or iridium. Both are rare, expensive and mostly imported. Indian scientists just found a way around both.
17. Her research has been cited 27,000 times by peers worldwide. In 2026, one of science's oldest honors finally caught up.
18. 205 unicorns overseas have an Indian-origin founder. Together, they're worth $560 billion.
19. Her friends pooled ₹40,000 so she could travel to Delhi. She came back Kerala's first tribal woman IAS officer.
20. September 24, 1940: born to a swimmer who'd cross the English Channel before anyone in Asia.
21. In 1995, she coined a term that changed how psychology understands prejudice. In 2026, the US named her one of its Great Immigrants for it.
22. She moved to America at 20 with $200. Now she's building the world's longest-range electric boat.
23. Indian Railways just commissioned its most advanced anti-collision system yet. It applies the brakes automatically - before a human even reacts.
24. She lost her father to cancer at one, dropped out after Class 10 and was married at 19. Now she earns ₹50 lakh a year - and trains 15,000 farmers for free.
25. September 25, 1920: the man India's own spaceport would later be named after was born.
26. Most Indian farmers can't afford their own drone. So the government's plan skips ownership entirely - and shares it instead.
27. An Indian fintech founder now runs the app 3 billion people use to talk to each other.
28. A medical mistake took her sight as an infant. She spent her life giving 200 other blind people their independence back.
29. September 26, 1820: born into scarcity, he became 'the Ocean of Learning' - then used it to fight his own caste.
30. He wanted to know why India's small-town councils keep underperforming. The answer won him one of political science's most prestigious awards.
31. She took up the sitar at age 8. By 2026, she'd been nominated for a Grammy 13 times.
32. India just finished a railway built for one purpose only: cargo. No passengers, no mixed traffic - just freight, moving faster than ever before.
33. He built an AI company from scratch. Jeff Bezos backed it. Forbes now values him at $2.1 billion.
34. He sold his own auto-rickshaw to afford a trip to the national championships. This year, he won India its first medal at the Commonwealth Games.
35. September 27, 1932: born in a city that would soon become another country - he'd go on to define Bollywood romance.
